ABB.name: ABB Migration
ABB.desc: ABB Freelance Migration Tool — turns an ABB Freelance 2016 CSV export into a DeltaV migration package, with no Freelance licence and no Freelance experience needed. Draws the FBD sheets so the logic can be read; says what each block becomes in DeltaV (PCSD module class, evidence, and a scan rate DeltaV will accept); and gives you the master tag list, IO list with target card types, signal cross-reference, alarm list, controller sizing and cross-controller signals — plus a coverage report of anything it could not decode.

DeltaV.name: LiveTools
DeltaV.desc: Desktop toolkit for DeltaV Live .ahc graphics files: tabular reports, an interactive editor with live rendering, bulk find/replace, thumbnail export, structural compare, project-wide library analysis, and localization.

DeltaV.name: DvHistExport
DeltaV.desc: Exports DeltaV Continuous Historian data — connects to a historian node, live tag search, reads raw samples over a time range, and exports to CSV. Pure-Python client over the DeltaV historian DLLs (32-bit).

DeltaV.name: SuperOPCWatchIt
DeltaV.desc: Advanced OPC-DA Tag Monitor for Emerson DeltaV. Live tag browsing, CSV import/export, write audit log.

DeltaV.name: DifFHX
DeltaV.desc: Compares two DeltaV FHX files and generates a diff report in Excel or PDF format.

DeltaV.name: FHXport
DeltaV.desc: Parses a DeltaV FHX file and generates 11 report types: Interlock, Alarm, IO, Module, EM, Reference, Historian, User Log, Phase, Named Set, PID Tuning.

DeltaV.name: FHXEdit
DeltaV.desc: Interactive tree editor for DeltaV FHX files with advanced find-and-replace, bulk delete, split, trim, and partial export.

DeltaV.name: WebFHX
DeltaV.desc: Converts a DeltaV FHX export into a portable standalone HTML viewer with hierarchy tree and optional FBD/SFC graphics.

DeltaV.name: EMTools
DeltaV.desc: Unified DeltaV Equipment Module toolkit — generate EMs from templates with a visual SFC logic editor, export/import class parameters as CSV, and auto-comment SFC steps, all over a shared document library.

DeltaV.name: FHXMerge
DeltaV.desc: Merges two or more DeltaV FHX files with element-level conflict resolution via a multi-pane diff interface.

DeltaV.name: FMTTools
DeltaV.desc: DeltaV user-defined import and export: build, export and validate format specifications and their data files. Replaces FMTMaker, FMTExport and ModExport.

DeltaV.name: CEMatrix
DeltaV.desc: Analyses a DeltaV FHX export to generate an interactive HTML interlock matrix and network graph.

DeltaV.name: TuningAid
DeltaV.desc: OPC UA-connected PID tuning tool with step testing, process characterisation, and live trending for DeltaV loops.

DeltaV.name: DvTwin
DeltaV.desc: DeltaV control system digital twin with OPC UA connectivity, FHX simulation, automated test runner, bulk import/export, and historian.

DeltaV.name: DVEmu
DeltaV.desc: Offline DeltaV emulator - runs an FHX config's control logic faithfully AND simulates the plant it controls, with 2D/3D live views and scenario/sweep/replay testing. No real DeltaV or OPC required.

DeltaV.name: FHXVerify
DeltaV.desc: Validates DeltaV FHX exports - reference, integrity, SFC, named-set, and DeltaV Module Analysis checks (MODE.ACTUAL, hardcoded confirms, name limits) with typo detection - and applies auto-fixes, with a browsable HTML report.

DeltaV.name: OPCBridge
DeltaV.desc: OPC DA to OPC UA bridge for DeltaV - native 32-bit COM interop to the DeltaV DA server, republished as an OPC UA server with live diagnostics.

DeltaV.name: Op2Live
DeltaV.desc: Converts DeltaV Operate graphics to DeltaV Live — a vendored Python port of Emerson's ConversionUtility wrapped in a guided pipeline (parse, scan, dynamo/contextual study, draft mappings, XSLT build/apply, verify, reports, polish, design specification and validation testing) with a visual mapping editor, GEM thumbnails, VBA→TypeScript translation, and a polish step that proposes merging near-identical pop-ups into shared contextual displays. Delivers a gap analysis, a design specification, the four validation gates, and reports covering graphic scope, display/module links, class and standard reuse, and merge recommendations.

DeltaV.name: OperateTools
DeltaV.desc: Native Rust toolkit for DeltaV Operate (iFix) graphic files — .grf pictures plus .fxg globals, .fds dynamo sets and .tbx toolbars (same format) — property/inventory/tag/animation/VBA reports (XLSX/CSV), iFix-style find & replace with automatic output validation, embedded-Python mass-edit scripting, expression repair (restores missing animation tag connections and resyncs stale source copies), PNG thumbnail rendering, structural + VBA source compare, and a Tag Groups tab to edit .tgd tag display groups (grid editor, bulk add/edit/delete across files with per-column Python transforms, @TOKEN@ cross-check).

DeltaV.name: VIMTools
DeltaV.desc: Reads Emerson/Mynah VimNet .vio configuration files for DeltaV Virtual I/O Modules - browse the VIM / controller / data-set tree, view EtherNet/IP buffer-to-signal mappings, and run read-only VIM diagnostics.

DeltaV.name: DvScan
DeltaV.desc: Explains why a DeltaV controller appears in the Decommissioned Nodes list and then vanishes, so you can decide what to do about it in DeltaV. A controller is kept in that list only while it announces redundancy role 2; one carrying an assigned identity announces role 0 and ages out in about two minutes, and can never be commissioned. DvScan reads the POWERUP tree, an FHX export of the configuration and the plug-and-play traffic, and says which of the three disagrees - marking every finding with the sources it rests on, because a claim from the disk alone is not the same as one three sources agree about. Every file DeltaV writes carries a timestamp this decodes, so two bindings claiming one node can be told apart by which was written first. Load a packet capture and it also finds controllers no other source can see: one sitting at its default address is in no device table, has no binding and has no download image, so only the wire knows it is there at all. It is a diagnostic with one exception, and that exception asks twice before it acts: DeltaV was captured decommissioning a controller, the message turns out to be broadcast and selected by MAC, and DvScan can replay it to make an orphan return to its default address and become commissionable again. Each verdict says what it means and what to check next.

DeltaV.name: DvVMManager
DeltaV.desc: DeltaV VM fleet cockpit — your whole DeltaV fleet in one rail, colour-coded by health, with curated one-click operations (export database, add user, download setup data, licence update), the Hyper-V/ESXi servers behind it, per-system power and checkpoints, file/account/process/network tools, fleet-wide file deployment (push or delete the same Operate graphics across every station at once), and local network diagnostics that say whether an unreachable system is really down or the path from this PC is broken. Replaces VMTools.

Provox.name: PvxIO
Provox.desc: Bidirectional converter for PROVOX IO configuration — export FHX to Excel (Files, Cards, Channels) or import Excel back to FHX.

Provox.name: PvxPDX
Provox.desc: Processes Provox PDX files to extract tables, FSTs, operations, and queries into human-readable output files.

Provox.name: PDXDiff
Provox.desc: Compares two folders of Provox PDX export data, generating a PDF summary and Excel change log of all differences.

Provox.name: FSTDecompiler
Provox.desc: GUI tool — decompiles Provox FST bytecode into human-readable pseudocode with a stage-by-stage viewer and syntax highlighting.

Provox.name: ODFDiff
Provox.desc: Diffs two HMI configuration directories, generating SVG overlays, interactive HTML screen reports, and Excel change logs.

Provox.name: PVXMigration
Provox.desc: Generates DeltaV migration deliverables from ProVOX configuration data — appendix tables (CSV), Basebuild (XLSX) and a Functional Requirements doc (DOCX).

Virtualization.name: VMCreds
Virtualization.desc: 4-stage tool for auditing, discovering accounts, bulk-updating passwords, and remediating scheduled tasks across Hyper-V VMs via WinRM.

Allen Bradley.name: ABComms
Allen Bradley.desc: GUI tool for communicating with Rockwell Allen-Bradley PLCs — tag read/write, tag browser, controller admin, and EDS-based chassis catalog lookup.

Allen Bradley.name: EDSCatalog
Allen Bradley.desc: Browser for CIP/EtherNet-IP EDS device files — resolves device identities to catalog numbers and lists configurable device parameters.

Allen Bradley.name: Logix2dv
Allen Bradley.desc: Rockwell Logix to DeltaV migration assistant - parses Studio 5000 L5X (and .ACD) exports, maps dependencies, and generates proposed DeltaV modules as importable FHX.

Allen Bradley.name: ABCommission
Allen Bradley.desc: EtherNet/IP device commissioning — a friendlier replacement for Rockwell's BootP-DHCP and Address Commissioning tools: discover devices (ListIdentity), assign IPs to factory-default devices via a built-in BOOTP/DHCP server, set the CIP TCP/IP config static, and read/write drive/adapter parameters. Probes a device to describe itself (identity, object-model scan, live self-describing parameter list with scaling) so no EDS or manual is needed for most devices.

Allen Bradley.name: FTViewTools
Allen Bradley.desc: Read a FactoryTalk View SE/ME application's displays without FactoryTalk View — no licence, no HMI server, no restored project. Scans a folder of .gfx files and reports every caption, step name and expression, every tag each display references, and which FactoryTalk Directory shortcut or data server it resolves through. Distinguishes a real tag from a #n parameter placeholder, cross-references a tag to the displays that use it, searches all display text at once, and flags shortcuts spelled inconsistently — the join between a graphic and a controller that nothing checks until an operator opens the screen. Exports CSV and a standalone HTML report.

CodeSys.name: STReader
CodeSys.desc: Converts IEC 61131-3 Structured Text programs into Process Flow Diagram HTML and PDF exports.

Documentation.name: CornerPDF
Documentation.desc: PDF reader, annotator, organiser and engineering review tool — read, mark up, assemble, redact and compare drawings and specifications without Acrobat. Markup with stamps and calibrated measurement; reorder/split/merge/compress pages; watermarks, Bates numbering and headers/footers; offline OCR that makes scans searchable; redaction that truly removes content; revision compare with a visual overlay; instrument-tag index cross-referenced against a DeltaV FHX export; drawing-package assembly with a linked index sheet; batch a folder. Fully offline.

Documentation.name: SuperDocs
Documentation.desc: Every help file you own in one searchable library — point it at a DeltaV node's Books Online folder and all ~116 .chm files become one index of 16,800 topics you can search at once, with a hit count per manual so you know whether the answer is in Batch, Control Studio, Diagnostics or the SIS books before you read a word. Reads compiled help (.chm) and the older WinHelp (.hlp) that Windows itself can no longer open, plus PDFs and folders of exported HTML — no vendor product installed, no internet and no add-in, because both decoders are built in. Full-text search across every book at once with per-book hit counts, quoted phrases, exclusions, wildcards and a regex mode for tag and loop numbers; every book's keyword index merged into one alphabet. Reader with tabs, light/dark/sepia, text scaling and find-on-page. Favourites, history and reading positions live in a separate file from the library, so re-importing a book never loses them and handing someone the library never hands over yours. Exports a page or a whole result set to a bookmarked PDF, a page to PNG, and chosen pages to a .sdoc share pack that opens in any browser with nothing installed. Also runs as a read-only MCP server so an assistant can search vendor documentation offline.

Documentation.name: P&ID Reader
Documentation.desc: Extracts tags, device types, symbols and connectivity from P&ID PDFs (OCR + OpenCV) into structured tables, instrument loops, QA overlays and a connectivity graph.

Documentation.name: P&ID Maker
Documentation.desc: Draws ISA-5.1 conformant P&IDs and exports them as searchable PDFs that carry their own tag database. Author from scratch, from a project spreadsheet (equipment list / line list / instrument index), from a DeltaV configuration, or from a P&ID Reader extraction. Live conformance checking as you draw.

Documentation.name: TableX
Documentation.desc: Extracts tables and text from any document — images, scanned/digital PDFs, Word, PowerPoint and HTML — into CSV/Excel. Fully offline OCR (RapidOCR), nothing uploaded.

Documentation.name: FnR
Documentation.desc: Multi-format find & replace across Word, Excel, PowerPoint, DeltaV FHX, Operate graphics, XML and text files — case-insensitive, whole-word and regex matching, a dry-run preview, and DeltaV unit replication that builds the map from an exported FHX.

AI.name: MP4Transcribe
AI.desc: Offline video/audio transcriber powered by OpenAI Whisper. Batch-transcribe files or whole folders to text or .srt/.vtt subtitles, with language selection, translate-to-English, and automatic GPU acceleration. FFMPEG bundled; nothing is uploaded.

AI.name: CornerCode
AI.desc: Fully offline AI assistant for automation engineers — a local Qwen2.5-Coder-7B model (bundled llama-server) drives guided, single-purpose tasks: research a manual or datasheet; fix an error, explain or review code, write tests, or write a script for a file that cannot leave the plant; read Rockwell, CODESYS or ABB PLC logic you did not write; turn a control narrative into requirements and review or edit documents and spreadsheets; and for DeltaV, ask your own FHX export, check custom logic, generate a FAT test plan from an FRS, draft Calc/Action/Condition expressions or EM logic for EMTools. Nothing is uploaded; the model, embeddings and runtime all ship in the box.

AI.name: SkillExplorer
AI.desc: Shared catalog of Cornerstone AI add-ons for Claude Code. Browse the skills and MCP servers, then install one in a click or export it as a shareable .zip. Skills install to ~/.claude/skills and ship their bundled command-line tools (reqgen, dv_converter); MCP servers are staged and registered with the client for you. Catalog: Control Narrative → Requirements, Describe DeltaV Modules, Generate EM Logic, plus the DeltaV FHX, Operate Graphics, OPC UA, Event Chronicle (alarms & events), Remote Windows and Emerson SMS servers.

Reverse Engineering.name: ByteWright
Reverse Engineering.desc: Binary file detective — auto-analyses unknown files (magic numbers, entropy, embedded data, PE/ELF/Mach-O/PDF/OLE/PCAP, YARA rules, disassembly) into a plain-language verdict. Fully offline.

Reverse Engineering.name: Patina
Reverse Engineering.desc: Native decompiler — lifts Windows PE and Linux ELF binaries to readable C using an x86 disassembler and a custom IR.

Remote.name: CornerRDP
Remote.desc: Deterministic RDP console + visual automation builder — reaches Windows/DeltaV/OT nodes that mstsc can but WinRM cannot (Standard RDP Security/RC4, TLS, NLA) via the vendored rdpilot engine. Manual cockpit: live desktop with click-to-click control and typing, session clipboard, file push/pull, run-as-SYSTEM commands, guest-agent deploy, reboot. Power-Automate-style Flow builder: sequence blocks (click, type, wait-for/assert element, run command, screenshot, if/repeat/for-each-target) with per-step retry, variables, and live point-and-click authoring — turn any repetitive RDP chore into a saved, multi-target automation. Saved connection profiles; passwords never persisted.

Comms.name: SuperComms
Comms.desc: Read live values from plant equipment over eleven protocols — OPC UA, classic OPC, Modbus, Allen-Bradley, MQTT, Siemens S7, REST, SOAP and SQL — with tags from different systems side by side on one clock. It can also act as the device, so you can test against a system that is not built yet.

Training.name: InstrumentLab
Training.desc: Learn process instruments by running them: 31 measuring technologies across level, flow, temperature, pressure, analytical, valves and pumps, every one simulated rather than described. Set the process and the installation on a workbench and watch the measurement respond, see the equations worked with your own numbers, and view each instrument as installed and in cutaway — where an unfilled wet leg, a thermowell in a dead leg or an orifice plate fitted backwards is visible, which it never is from the outside. Diagnose-it lessons put you in front of a real complaint with a time budget: every observation costs simulated minutes, and naming the right fault without taking the observation that proves it is scored as a guess. Nothing here touches a plant.
